prompt: A clean, straight-on printed raffle/lottery number sheet titled 'STAFF SOCIAL CLUB PRIZE DRAW'. Subtitle 'This week's issued draw numbers (no number repeats)'. Print SIXTY two-digit ticket numbers arranged in a neat grid of 6 rows by 10 columns, each number in its own boxed cell, large and legible. Use EXACTLY these sixty numbers, in this order, filling the grid left-to-right then top-to-bottom: 76 68 38 99 48 25 67 29 44 65 90 19 69 79 93 66 78 35 11 51 73 23 01 80 34 52 83 14 64 24 31 97 88 09 42 54 55 46 86 53 27 06 98 07 62 26 81 60 91 63 72 39 87 40 15 21 18 04 12 58. CRITICAL: every one of the sixty numbers must be DIFFERENT -- no value may appear twice anywhere on the sheet. Print exactly sixty boxed two-digit numbers, nothing else.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a printed raffle/lottery sheet showing a grid of two-digit ticket numbers. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed grid of numbers? A photo, scan or clean sheet all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is a blank card, plain panel, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_count: How many two-digit numbers are printed on this sheet? Give a whole number only.

steps.read_crop: This sheet prints a grid of two-digit ticket numbers, each in its own cell.
